about: Milliseconds per step: what each step takes on a TYPICAL GitHub runner
(ubuntu-latest), the machine CI packs for. Only the shard packing in
tools/run-tests.mjs reads them (run-tests-parallel.mjs prints their sum).
No test behaviour depends on them: a step missing from this table is packed
at the median, not skipped - and that is not harmless, so new steps carry
an estimate (last line) until a CI run measures them.
WHERE THESE CAME FROM (2026-10-22, ci-stability). Every shard SUMMARY table
of Tests #297-#305, 1,282 step times (#301 shard 7 and #305 shard 4 were
cancelled at the job timeout and left none; #305 shards 6 and 7 were not
read), with two corrections:
FRESH ONLY. A time counts only if nothing `run-tests.mjs --touching` links
to its step changed between its run's commit and 6f3354f: support:shells'
188 s from before supports-print-1 (#256) is not its 1,222 s after, and
#305 (claude-wip-next with #261-#264) counts only for the 72 steps they
leave alone. 40 steps rest on one run, the rest on two to nine.
RUNNER-NORMALISED. Most shards ran within a few % of each other; about one
in five (#297 2-3, #299 1 and 6, #301 5, #302 4-5) ran the same steps in
0.6-0.7 of the time, a few others in 0.85-0.9. Each time is scaled by its
shard's speed (the median, over its steps of 20 s and more, of the step's
time against its median across all nine runs) to the typical runner's.
Unscaled, the 13 steps that only a fast shard measured fresh were ~40 %
light: support:workflow 338 s for ~550.
These summed to 13,808 s over 257 steps. ci-shard-split (below) cut three of
them into seven; the 261 sum to 13,484 s and pack twenty shards at ~674 s
each: ~11 min of tests on a typical runner, ~7 on a fast one. The heaviest
step is support:shells-clamp, 467 s; sixteen shards would pack at 843 s,
over run-tests.mjs SHARD_BUDGET_S (700 s).
THE SEVEN (ci-shard-split). support:shells (1,229 s), gscope:speed (650 s) and
support:interface (184 s) are three scripts still, run whole by hand, and no
longer steps. Their CI times above were apportioned to the new steps by each
one's local time (mean of 3-4 runs) times the parent's CI-over-local:
shells 1,229/1,908 s, speed 650/732 s, interface 184/290 s.
support:shells-* also slice a support's three variants on worker threads
(tools/nso_slice_pool.js), so their sum (702 s) is under the parent's 1,229 s;
gscope:speed-* each open the 203k-move file, so theirs (840 s) is over the
parent's 650 s. `--weights-from` replaces all seven after the first green run.
RE-MEASURE FROM THE CSV, NOT BY HAND. Every CI run uploads timing.csv (its
"npm test" job merges a row per step - step, shard, seconds, result - from
the shards). `node tools/run-tests.mjs --weights-from timing.csv[,b.csv]`
rewrites this table from it: the mean of each step's passing rows, each
shard scaled to the typical runner the same way, and the file named in
this file's "source". Two runs averaged beat one. Then check
`node tools/run-tests.mjs --shard-plan`, which has no wall clock in it.
A SNAPSHOT, NOT A CONSTANT. Steps get slower as they grow and runners vary:
the symptom of drift is uneven shard totals (--merge-timing prints them)
and, past a point, a shard nearing the job timeout. Locally these are NOT
this machine's times (a local box is faster than a typical runner), so
run-tests-parallel.mjs draws no speedup ratio from their sum.
CI-SHARD-SPLIT-2. gscope:speed-drag, support:shells-clamp, support:workflow,
connect:drive, pick:release, rotate:handles, zoom:drive, gcode:gscope-zoom and
findings:drive are scripts still, run whole by hand, and no longer steps: the
23 steps that replace them are in testSteps (--only= on each script; the
partition is asserted in the script where the groups share code). Weights are
ESTIMATES: the parent's CI weight apportioned by each new step's local time
(apportioned, not measured, so the sum is the parent's), less the real work cut:
the silence tests at a sixth of the watchdog (~145 s), rotate:handles' lap at 3
degrees a move (~106 s), zoom:drive's 2 wheel steps each way (~80 s). The plan is
13,840 s, 692 s a shard. Over ~250 s still: gscope:speed-drag-file (579),
support:shells-clamp-a1 (305), lift:plate (281): each is one chain that cannot
be cut without repeating its setup or breaking a gate. `--weights-from` replaces
all of them after the first green run.
Steps merged after Tests #305 carry their own branch's estimate until a CI
run measures them:
(how each estimate was made is that step's own "note" in this file)
